title: Multi-city union protest against Milei labor reform, central gathering before Congress
location: Buenos Aires (central gathering before Congress); article also reports demonstrations in principal cities without enumerating them
scope: One reported multi-city protest action; local-city boundaries/count ownership unresolved
organizer: CGT called the demonstration; CTA branches, transport/state/metalworker/other unions and political groups reportedly participated
protesters: Union members, workers, pensioners and political/social groups (as reported)
participants_original: Article states “miles de personas” at protests in Argentina’s principal cities; Buenos Aires is named as central gathering but its local attendance is not separately counted.
threshold_50_evidence: The article’s plural “miles” supports 50+ at the national multi-city action scale; no city-specific threshold can be attributed to Buenos Aires from this account alone.

date.evidence: Article dated Feb 11 2026 at 05:40 CET and describes “este miércoles”; it reports protest from midday before Congress.

location.evidence: Article says central mobilization began at midday in Buenos Aires in front of Congress and separately describes protests in principal cities.

protest_action.evidence: Body says thousands manifested against the labor reform promoted by the Milei government.

organizer.evidence: Article identifies CGT as convener, with CTA branches and other unions/groups.

state_target.evidence: The demonstration opposed the labor-reform bill promoted by the national government.

demands.evidence: Article quotes the CGT saying the reform reduces rights, precarizes labor and lowers wages.

participants.evidence: “Miles de personas” is stated for the principal cities nationally; no Buenos Aires-specific number is given.

response.evidence: Subtitle reports two detained; body says more than ten detained per official sources and four police agents injured per official sources. Preserve the discrepancy.

violence.evidence: Article reports that a group of protesters threw stones and Molotov cocktails at police; it describes police responding with tear gas and rubber bullets. The preceding union demonstration is described as peaceful until then.

open_questions: Are other principal-city actions part of one national multi-site unit or separately codable local events?
Can attendance be localized to Buenos Aires?
Can the arrest-count discrepancy be resolved?
proposal_limitations: Candidate from one directly read report; no independent corroboration. National-scale wording is not apportioned to Buenos Aires. Protester violence is attributed to a group at the close of an otherwise peaceful march, not to all participants. No official approval.
